title: A singular surface with free tangent sheaf
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The construction, after OpenAI's 2026 manuscript, of a normal affine complex surface whose module of derivations is free of rank two although the surface is singular: a counterexample to the Lipman-Zariski conjecture. Derivations, the characteristic-p counterexample and products; an explicit elliptic curve on the quadric with a line bundle of order four and a quadratic form on its sections; a curve of genus 21 with fourth-order contact and a fourth root of its canonical bundle; traces, the residue theorem and Grothendieck's splitting theorem on the projective line; the trace form and the residue data; gluing two vector fields order by order near the curve; analytic realization, contraction and the free derivation module; algebraization by finite determinacy with relations.
prerequisites: Kahler differentials, smooth algebras and the Jacobian criterion, regular local rings, Serre's normality criterion, completion, Artin-Rees and henselization (course Commutative algebra for geometry, AG-CA)
cohomology of O(a,b) on P^1 x P^1, Serre duality and the canonical bundle, Serre's theorems and comparison theorems (course Cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves, AG-QC)
Riemann-Roch for smooth projective curves (course The abstract theory of ideals, NOE-ABS, lesson 6, Theorem 4.3)
holomorphic functions of several variables, coherence, the analytic Nullstellensatz, Theorems A and B on Stein manifolds (course Complex analytic spaces and coherent sheaves)

open_obligations: N1 Grauert's contraction theorem (Math. Ann. 146 (1962), section 4.8(e)): a compact connected smooth curve with negative self-intersection in a complex surface has a neighbourhood with a proper map onto a normal complex space contracting the curve to a point, biholomorphic elsewhere, with pi_* O = O. Used in lesson 8, Lemma 3.1. Intended home: a lesson of Complex analytic spaces and coherent sheaves.

N2 Grauert's direct image theorem (Publ. Math. IHES 5 (1960), section 6, Hauptsatz I): higher direct images of coherent sheaves under proper holomorphic maps are coherent. Used in lesson 8, Lemma 3.1 and Section 5. Intended home: Complex analytic spaces and coherent sheaves.

N3 The analytic theorem on formal functions (Grauert 1960, section 6, Hauptsatz IIa). Used in lesson 8, Lemma 3.1 and Section 5. Intended home: Complex analytic spaces and coherent sheaves (the algebraic version is AG-QC, The theorem on formal functions).

N4 Stein neighbourhood bases of points of complex spaces and Cartan's Theorem B on Stein spaces (Seminaire Cartan 4 (1951/52), expose 18); the programme proves Theorem B for Stein manifolds only. Used in lesson 8, Lemma 3.1.
N5 Extension of holomorphic functions across a point of a normal complex surface (Demailly, Complex analytic and differential geometry, Chapter II, Corollary 7.8). Used in lesson 8, Proposition 4.1.

A1 Artin's approximation theorem (Publ. Math. IHES 36 (1969), Theorem 1.10; Stacks Tag 07QY). Used in lesson 9, Proposition 3.1. Intended home: a lesson after AG-CA, Henselian local rings and henselization.

A2 Excellence of convergent power series rings over C (EGA IV, Remark 7.8.4(v), proved in section 18) and the permanence properties of EGA IV, Scholium 7.8.3(ii),(v): the completion of a normal complex analytic local ring is a normal domain. Used in lesson 9, Proposition 3.1.

Not in the course: the theorem of Biswas, Gurjar and Kolte (logarithmic Kodaira dimension) and the universal property of blowups along modules, quoted in lesson 9 for two consequences that are not used elsewhere.
